Intermediaries [Roles]: TRAFFIC International (Lead implementing organization, providing technical support/trainings, guidance, and project implementation), Bac Kan Provincial Forest Protection Department (FPD) (Protecting medicinal and aromatic plants, control of MAP trade, liaison and providing support/instructions to management board), People Resources and Conservation Foundation (PRCF) Viet Nam (Build upon and complement CEPF-funded projects, complete market assessment report), Management board of Nam Xuan Lac Species and Habitat Conservation Area (Daily protection of MAPs, technical guidance for local villagers towards sustainable harvesting, enforcement, encouraging local collectors), Bac Kan Traditional Medicine Association and Bac Kan Provincial Department of Health (Assist local collectors to obtain certificate on sustainable harvesting, training for local people, widen awareness of project activities), Local Peopleâ€™s Committee of Xuan Lac and Ban Thi Communes (Facilitate and monitor local collectors applying sustainable harvesting and processing techniques, control trade of target species between collectors and traders, establish inspection team), Helvetas - Swiss Association for International Cooperation (BioTrade project implementer, exchange project experiences), Vietnam Association of Traditional Medicinal Materials (National commitment to establish a network of traditional medicine shops/clinics interested in sustainably collected wild medicine products), Centre of Plant Conservation (CPC) / Dr. Nguyen Tap (Conduct resource assessment and management plan for target species)
Beneficiaries: Local collectors from Dao and Tay ethnic minority groups (particularly women); 104 trained collectors (51 villagers in May 2012 and 53 collectors in January 2013); 103 households practicing sustainable harvesting techniques across 7 villages (Ban Tun, Ban Eng, Keo Nang, Phja Khao, Khuoi Ken, Ban Na Da, Ban Khang) in Xuan Lac and Ban Thi Communes; 7 collection groups formed. Specific threatened flagship flora protected include Amomum villosum Lour, Amomum xanthioides var. xanthioides, Alpinia malaccensis, Alpinia latilabris, Alpinia menghaiensis, Aristolochia kwangsiensis, Podophyllum tonkinense, and Asarum caudigerum.
Location (focussed area): Total of 9,296 hectares (1,788 hectares core zone and 7,508 hectares buffer zone) located in Nam Xuan Lac Species and Habitat Conservation Area, Xuan Lac and Ban Thi Communes, Bac Kan Province, Northern Limestone, Vietnam.
Commodity [solution-oriented]: Development of sustainable wild collection of Medicinal and Aromatic Plants (MAPs) model; implementation of FairWild and Fairtrade Principles; development of co-management mechanisms and a benefit-sharing mechanism; creation of 7 collection groups/cooperatives; provision of value-addition post-harvest technologies including two village-shared steel herb dryers and three brick dryers; development of management plans with sustainable harvesting quotas; provision of real-time market information and prices to collectors; establishment of a conservation and livelihood support fund contributing 5% of profits.
Ecosystem Services: Supporting: Protection of habitat and refuge for threatened wild Medicinal and Aromatic Plants (MAPs) (including Aristolochia kwangsiensis, Podophyllum tonkinense, Asarum caudigerum), biodiversity conservation, and regeneration of Alpinia and Amomum species in limestone forests. Provisioning: Sustainable harvesting and supply of wild medicinal and aromatic plants (Alpinia and Amomum species) for alternative income generation and stable livelihood for forest-dependent communities; provision of high-quality dried raw medicinal materials. Cultural: Empowerment of vulnerable ethnic minority groups (Tay and Dao people), particularly women, in community-based decision-making; improved traditional knowledge and natural resource management through co-management mechanisms; participatory capacity building and fair-trade mechanisms.

Name: Cat Ba
Fund Provider: Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund (CEPF) [$70,000]; Australian National University (ANU) [US$8,400]; WildInvest [US$9,967]; Mohammed bin Zayed [US$6,000]; Margot Marsh [US$2,072]
Intermediaries [Roles]: Fauna & Flora International (FFI) [Project design, grantee, coordination, technical inputs]; Cat Ba National Park Management Board [Designated government authority managing the park, facilitating partner work, providing staff for research/monitoring, Chair of Technical Working Group]; Cat Ba Langur Conservation Project (CBLCP) [Implementation of all project activities, population monitoring]; Australian National University (ANU) School of Archaeology and Anthropology [Leading the scientific research agenda, collection of behavioural, ecological, and genetic data, provision of PhD students]; Cat Ba Langur Technical Working Group (CBLTWG) [Multi-stakeholder centralized decision-making forum]; IUCN Conservation Breeding Specialist Group [Conducted independent Population Viability Analysis]; Hai Phong DARD, Hai Phong DoNRE, Department of Nature Conservation at MARD, BCA at MoNRE [Government representatives on TWG]; Endangered Primate Rescue Center, IUCN Primate Specialist Group, IEBR, CRES HUS [Technical expert members on TWG]
Beneficiaries: Cat Ba langur / golden-headed langur (Trachypithecus poliocephalus poliocephalus) [Critically Endangered flagship species protected]; 3 PhD students (Rebecca Hendershott, Kirrily Apthorpe, Kayla Ruskin) and 1 MSc student (Ta Tuyet Nga) [Supported for academic research]; Vietnamese nationals (including National Park Director Mr Hoang Van Thap and Mai Sy Luan) [Supported through capacity building and translations of research documents]; Cat Ba NP rangers and FPD staff [Engaged in monitoring and population surveys]; Decision-makers at local, provincial, and central levels [Benefited from technical knowledge transfer on population management]
Location (focussed area): Cat Ba National Park, Cat Hai district, Hai Phong City, Vietnam (Specifically: Cua Dong area, the Sanctuary, Hang Cai, Cai Minh Tu - Viet Hai). N/A for exact spatial footprint size in hectares or square kilometers.
Commodity [solution-oriented]: Cat Ba Langur Technical Working Group (CBLTWG) governance platform; Population Viability Analysis (PVA) and models; Comprehensive population survey frameworks and manual in Vietnamese; Targeted scientific research program addressing socioecology, feeding ecology, and habitat preference; Translated technical dossiers and documentation; incorporation of the TWG model into the National Action Plan for Vietnam's Primates
Ecosystem Services: Supporting: Habitat refuge for the critically endangered Cat Ba langur (Trachypithecus poliocephalus poliocephalus), protection of limestone karst habitats, conservation of the overall biodiversity of the Cat Ba Archipelago, and improved understanding of keystone plant species (43 plant taxa identified in diet). Provisioning: N/A. Cultural: N/A.

Name: Bac Me
Fund Provider: Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund (CEPF) (Grant Amount: US$400,000.0). Additional funding providers (Total: US$273,755): Great Apes conservation fund of US Fish and Wildlife Services (USFW) (US$20,023 for Conservation of Tonkin snub-nosed monkey in Tung Vai), AZA Ape TAG (US$30,000 for Capacity building for Trung Khanh Cao Vit gibbon conservation), Twycross Zoo (US$6,960 for Salaries for CCTs in Trung Khanh for conservation of Cao Vit gibbon), FOTA (US$26,600 for Capacity development for co-management and conservation of western black-crested gibbon), Co-management Learning Network (CMLN) (US$10,833 to Strengthen co-management approach), Global Trees Campaign (GTC) (US$173,339 for Conservation of priority tree species Magnolias and conifers), and the Arcus Foundation (for development of conservation action plans for Cao Vit gibbon).
Intermediaries [Roles]: Fauna & Flora International (FFI) [Project Implementing Organization and Sub-grant provider], Centre for Plant Conservation (CPC) [Implementing components related to tree conservation at the selected sites and operating community nurseries], University of Colorado Boulder [Conducting monitoring and research on the Tonkin snub-nosed monkey in Khau Ca SHCA core zone], People Resources and Conservation Foundation (PRCF) [Leading habitat (forest) restoration work], Denver Zoo [Conducting education activities in surrounding villages of Khau Ca SHCA], Management Advisory Committees (MACs) / Tonkin Snub-nosed Monkey and Magnolia Management Committee [Broadening and improving decision making of protected areas and multi-stakeholders engagement in PA management], Community Conservation Teams (CCTs) [Species monitoring, forest patrolling and supporting law enforcement], Forest Protection Departments (FPD) and Management Boards [Centralized data management, law enforcement, and protected area management].
Beneficiaries: Local communities in 13 villages around Trung Khanh and 7 villages around Khau Ca. 243 households provided with mobile fuel efficient stoves; 70 households received VA06 grass seedlings. 10 CCT members in Tung Vai, 10 CCT members in Khau Ca, and 6 CCT members in Trung Khanh trained and employed. Secondary school students in Quan Ba and Trung Khanh engaged in outdoor environmental education. Total 280 men and 140 women benefiting from formal training and increased income. Flagship fauna/flora protected: Tonkin snub-nosed monkey (117-121 individuals in Khau Ca, 15-21 individuals in Tung Vai), Cao Vit gibbon (124-136 individuals), Magnolia grandis, Magnolia citrata, Magnolia megaphylla, Magnolia tonkinensis, Taxus chinensis, Tsuga chinensis, Nageia fleuryi, Pinus kwantungensis, Cupressus tonkinensis, Xanthocyparis vietnamensis, and Magnolia coriacea.
Location (focussed area): Tung Vai Forest (VNM100): 5,000 hectares in Tung Vai commune, Quan Ba district, Ha Giang province; Khau Ca Species Habitat Conservation Area (VNM50): 2,014 hectares (also cited as 2,024 ha) in Tung Ba commune, Vi Xuyen district and Yen Dinh and Minh Son communes, Bac Me district, Ha Giang province; Trung Khanh SHCA (VNM98): 5,736 hectares (plus 4,079 ha in neighboring protection forest buffer zone) in Ngoc Con, Ngoc Khe and Phong Nam communes, Trung Khanh district, Cao Bang province.
Commodity [solution-oriented]: Community Conservation Teams (CCTs) utilizing Spatial Monitoring and Reporting Tool (SMART) for forest patrols; Management Advisory Committees (MACs); Species Conservation Action Plans (SCAPs) and Transboundary Conservation Action Plans; 243 mobile fuel efficient stoves; 2.17 ha of Elephant grass (VA06) silage technology for cattle feed; Metal waterwheel technology (45 wooden waterwheels replaced with metal frames); Community tree nurseries for propagation of tree saplings/cuttings.
Ecosystem Services: Supporting: Habitat restoration, biodiversity monitoring, and long-term conservation of priority CR primate populations (Tonkin snub-nosed monkey, Cao Vit gibbon) and threatened tree species (magnolias, conifers). Provisioning: Alternative cattle feed (elephant grass silage) reducing free livestock grazing impacts, fuel efficient stoves saving 40-60% of fuelwood, reduced hardwood timber extraction through metal waterwheel implementation. Cultural: Environmental education programmes in secondary schools, community co-management empowerment, awareness raising via calendar distribution, and capacity building for local conservation actors.
